title: Sample call rate

blocks.what_we_do: We keep only samples with a call rate of at least 98%. We apply this rule after the rough cleaning.
blocks.why:
The call rate of a sample is the share of its sites that were read successfully. A threshold (cut-off value) of 98% means at most 2% missing results. It does not mean 98% missing results.

A sample with a low call rate gives less information. This reduces the effective sample size, which is the amount of usable data. A low call rate can also be associated with a laboratory group or a recruitment group.

In another study, look at the distribution of call rates before you choose a threshold.
blocks.you_need: State 3.1 and the call-rate definition from step 2.4.
blocks.command:
```{r s3-2}
# 1. Remove samples with more than 2% of calls missing.
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "3.1"), "--mind", "0.02", "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "3.2")))
# Course bookkeeping: records the counts for the next step. Do not change.
ops <- guided_replay_lists(cfg, "3.2", "3.1")
guided_register(cfg, "3.2", "3.1", 1971, 296360, operations = ops)
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-1_state --mind 0.02 --make-pgen --out results/guided/s3-2_state --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

`--mind 0.02` removes samples with more than 2% missing calls. This is the same as a call rate below 98%. `--pfile`, `--make-pgen`, `--out`, `--threads` and `--memory` have the meanings given at step 3.1.

blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the input file named in the message and the previous step. Keep the command and the console messages. Do not use files from a different version of the dataset. See [troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.what_this_check_can_reveal: Moderate sample failures that the rough screen did not catch. Missingness can be associated with the [phenotype](docs/glossary.md#phenotype), here case or control status (a case has the disease, a control does not). It can also be associated with a [batch](docs/glossary.md#batch-effect), which is a group of samples processed together. For this reason, write down every exclusion.
blocks.quick_check:
A well has 1% missing calls. What is its call rate? Does it pass this rule?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

The call rate is 99%. The well passes the 98% call-rate rule.

</details>
blocks.files_created: `s3-2_state.*`, the list of removed samples and the replay metadata.
blocks.try_other_thresholds:
This box is not part of the main path. No later step uses it. It does not change your results.

The call rate of a sample is the share of its calls that are not missing. `--mind 0.02` removes samples with more than 2% missing calls, which is a call rate below 98%. A lower limit keeps more samples but lets in samples with poor DNA. A higher limit removes more samples and may throw away good data. A call rate of 95% to 98% is a common choice in genome-wide studies, and 98% is the stricter end of it. Each trial starts from the cohort saved at 3.1 and changes the limit only.

```{r s3-2_thresholds, eval=FALSE}
# Optional. Each trial starts from the same input and changes one threshold only.
thresholds <- c(0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20)
trial <- threshold_counts(cfg, guided_path(cfg, "3.1"), "--mind", thresholds)
trial$course_value <- trial$threshold == 0.02
trial
# Plot the removed samples. The course value is the large diamond.
plot_threshold_trials(trial, "Samples removed")
# Optional: add engine = "ggplot2" to plot_threshold_trials() to draw the plot with ggplot2 (install.packages("ggplot2") once first).
```

Plain PLINK 2 command for one trial. It writes only small files with the name that you give to `--out`, never a new dataset:

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-1_state --mind 0.05 --make-just-psam --out results/trials/s3-2_trial --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

The log file `results/trials/s3-2_trial.log` states how many samples were removed. To repeat the trial, change the number after `--mind` and use a new `--out` name.

The expected result of the trials:

| Threshold | Samples removed | Samples remaining |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.01 | 118 | 1,895 |
| **0.02 (course value)** | 42 | 1,971 |
| 0.05 | 0 | 2,013 |
| 0.1 | 0 | 2,013 |
| 0.2 | 0 | 2,013 |

How to read it. At 0.02 the course removes 42 wells. At 0.05 none are removed, so all 42 wells have between 2% and 5% missing calls. At 0.01 another 76 wells go (118 in total). The step is a clear case of a choice: the course value removes the wells that are poor but not broken.

Expected plot. For `--mind`, the horizontal axis shows the threshold and the vertical axis shows the number of samples removed. A red diamond marks the course value (0.02), where 42 samples are removed. The line joins the points in the order of the thresholds, so you can see how fast the count changes. The same plot with ggplot2 looks the same and has a light grid.

options.name: --make-pgen
options.explanation_markdown: `--make-pgen` saves the result as a new fileset (a saved state).

options.name: --memory
options.explanation_markdown: `--memory 2048` sets the memory limit to 2048 MiB (about 2 gigabytes).

options.name: --mind
options.explanation_markdown: `--mind 0.02` removes samples with more than 2% missing calls.

options.name: --out
options.explanation_markdown: `--out` sets the name prefix of the output files.

options.name: --pfile
options.explanation_markdown: `--pfile` selects the input fileset in the PLINK 2 native format.

options.name: --threads
options.explanation_markdown: `--threads 2` limits the number of worker threads (parallel jobs).

student_summary: We remove samples with more than 2% of their genotype calls missing. This keeps samples with enough information for the later analysis.
